Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i'm putting together the arrival information for site 14, and the power connection details are a bit hard to follow. could you review the entry in this file and make the wording clearer for the next camper:
north-gate-notes.md
The site is listed as having a 30-amp connection, and our extension cable is 25 feet long. Please keep those as separate details, since 30 amps is the connection rating and 25 feet is the cable length. I don't know whether the receptacle is working right now, so don't state that it has been tested or that it is working. Could you make the note say that campers should check the outlet before plugging in? Also, would you clarify that the cable we have is 25 feet, not that the hookup is 25 feet away? I want the entry to tell people what information we have without implying anything about the current condition of the connection. The outlet check should remain a request, not a claim that someone has already checked it. The details are meant to help people understand the hookup before they arrive, but I don't want the note to suggest that we know more than this.", "output": "I'm putting together the arrival information for site 14, and the power connection details are unclear. Could you review the entry in this file and make the wording clearer for the next camper?
north-gate-notes.md
The site is listed as having a 30-amp connection, and our extension cable is 25 feet long. Please keep these as separate details: 30 amps is the connection rating, and 25 feet is the cable length. I don't know whether the receptacle is working right now, so don't say it has been tested or is working. Please clarify that campers should check the outlet before plugging in, and that the cable we have is 25 feet long—not that the hookup is 25 feet away. The entry should share only the information we have without implying anything about the connection's current condition. Keep the outlet check as a request, not a claim that someone has already checked it. These details are meant to help people understand the hookup before they arrive, without suggesting that we know more than this."}]
